items.text: – No. As long as this thread is in your hand, you won't get lost. The other end is in my hand. This way you won't get lost.
items.q: Maman reassures her four-year-old with a thread game. Does it sound like a mother talking to a small child?
before: Maman always said:

items.text: – I found you four times. Now come here, my good boy. Come take this and walk around inside the house.
items.q: Maman plays hide-and-seek with her four-year-old. Does 'my good boy' sound warm and natural?
before: I moved away from the hole. Maman went dark. Maman always went dark, then bright again, four times. She'd always say:

items.text: – Good, my clever boy. When something scares you, use a trick so you don't get scared.
items.q: Maman praises her small son's trick for not being scared. Does it sound natural?
before: I always used a trick. Instead of the red door, I looked at the wall of the house next to it. It was white. Maman said:

items.text: – You didn't say.
items.q: A small boy, in tears, answers his brother's scolding. Does it sound like a small child?
before: Omid was crying. He said:

items.text: – Sure, you come on the mission too, but you have to be really careful. The stages are really hard.
items.q: Ghassem lets his little brother join the pretend mission. Does it sound like a child?
before: Ghassem said:

items.text: – Lots of people fail here. They go left.
items.q: Ghassem, playing commander, warns about a wrong turn. Does it sound like a child's game?
before: I never learned this part. He'd always say the most important... something... of the mission. Then he'd say:

items.text: – Our school is at the end. The last house. If we make noise, the teacher will hit our hands with a ruler.
items.q: Does this sound like a schoolboy talking to his little brothers?
before: Ghassem would say some more things. Then he'd say:

items.text: – It's old age, neighbor.
items.q: An old grocer with shaking hands says this to Maman. Does it sound natural?
before: We stood by Haaj Kazem's grocery. Ghassem always waved to him. Haaj Kazem always shakes his hands. When we go there with Maman, he shakes them too. He shakes the chickpeas fast-fast. He keeps pouring too many onto the scale, then taking some back. That day he said to Maman:

items.text: – If you get tired, don't come on the mission anymore.
items.q: Ghassem answers his tired little brother. Does it sound like a child?
before: – Ugh, I'm tired.
Ghassem said:

items.text: – I have no time at all this week. Next week, Thursday at three, the same place we met last time. I should also say I only have half an hour to spare.
items.q: Niloofar writes a cool, brisk reply to Amir. Does her note sound natural?
before: …said to Niloofar, I tell myself that if Niloofar did not accept me, it was not because of my words, but more because of my insistence on secrecy and because I never, neither before revealing my feelings nor after expressing them, went straight toward Niloofar inside the department. She had written:

items.text: – No one's room has a carpet, Baba-jan. Only we have a carpet, and that's because we're the elite room.
items.q: Eskandar shows off the room to his visiting father. Does this sound natural?
before: Niloofar heard my murmurs. When I entered the room, the boys from the room and an older man whom I guessed was Eskandar's Baba were sitting on the carpet in the middle of the room. It was past noon, and the declining sunlight had lit the middle of the carpet. Eskandar was saying:

items.text: – I vowed that if he gets better, I'll walk to Mashhad as a pilgrim.
items.q: Maman makes a religious vow for her sick son. Does it sound natural?
before: …sitting in the hall in front of the television, cracking sunflower seeds, and Maman seated beside him. The news spoke of the damage from widespread flooding in the northern and western provinces. From behind, Maman appeared to me as a small circle seated beside a larger rectangle. Maman was saying:

items.text: – You're all like my own children.
items.q: An old woman welcomes the students into her home. Does it sound warm and natural?
before: …and have tea and fruit while things calmed down outside. Two unfamiliar voices, speaking for all of us, said we couldn't impose any further. The old woman's insistence got nowhere and she went upstairs. A few minutes later she returned with a bowl of fruit and a pitcher of water. She was saying:

items.text: – Amir, Grandpa caught Covid too, but you'd never know it; he shook it off like a simple cold. Probably because he can't hear and has no idea what's going on, and he never got scared.
items.q: Amir's sister tells him how Grandpa got through Covid. Does it sound natural?
before: Mahboubeh says:

items.text: – I mean, did you pass?
items.q: Maman asks about his doctoral defense and hears there is no grade. Does her follow-up sound natural?
before: I say:
– There's no grade, Nini-jan.

items.text: – This is even better than Stadio delle Alpi.
items.q: A schoolboy compares their playing spot to a famous football stadium. Does it sound like a boy?
before: …that day on, in our eyes, that asphalt street was better than the dirt pitch we called Quchan's Stadio delle Alpi. Neither that day nor in the days that followed did our feet carry us beyond the white-plastered walls of that house and its yellow door. No farther one way or the other. Taghi said:

items.text: – So you're all very clever boys.
items.q: Eskandar, a little older, responds to the boys' bragging. Does it sound dry and natural?
before: Eskandar said:

items.text: At best, the dorm monitors got blue wall-to-wall carpeting instead of the dust-colored kind.
items.q: Eskandar, impressed by their carpet, compares other dorm rooms. Does this read naturally?
before: – Oh, so that's why. I'd never seen a room with a proper carpet before.

items.text: – Sure, our Baba-jan really hungers for respect.
items.q: Ghassem mocks their father's pride. Does 'really hungers for respect' sound natural and ironic?

items.text: – Now say whatever you want, but keep the final beit in mind.
items.q: Niloofar hands him the book after reading him a poem. Does her line sound natural?
